{{Short description|Swiss mathematician}}
'''Jürg Peter Buser''', known as Peter Buser, (born 27 February 1946 in [[Basel]]) is a Swiss mathematician, specializing in differential geometry and global analysis.

==Education and career==
Buser received his doctorate in 1976 from the [[University of Basel]] with advisor Heinz Huber and thesis ''Untersuchungen über den ersten Eigenwert des Laplaceoperators auf kompakten Flächen'' (Studies on the [[Dirichlet eigenvalue|first eigenvalue of the Laplace operator on compact surfaces]]).<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=85148|name =Jürg Peter Buser}}</ref> As a post-doctoral student he was at the [[University of Bonn]], the [[University of Minnesota]]. and the [[State University of New York at Stony Brook]], before he habilitated at the University of Bonn with a thesis on the length spectrum of [[Riemann surface]]s.

Buser is known for his construction of curved isospectral surfaces (published in 1986 and 1988). His 1988 construction led to a negative solution to [[Mark Kac]]'s famous 1966 problem ''[[Can one hear the shape of a drum?]]''. The negative solution was published in 1992 by [[Scott Wolpert]], [[David Webb (mathematician)|David Webb]] and [[Carolyn S. Gordon]].<ref name="GordonWebb1992">{{cite journal|last1=Gordon|first1=Carolyn|last2=Webb|first2=David L.|last3=Wolpert|first3=Scott|title=One Cannot Hear the Shape of a Drum|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|volume=27|issue=1|year=1992|pages=134–139|issn=0273-0979|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1992-00289-6|doi-access=free|arxiv=math/9207215}}</ref><ref>Barry Cipra: '' You can't always hear the shape of a drum '', in '' What´s happening in the Mathematical Sciences '', volume 1, American Mathematical Society 1993, p. 15</ref> The {{ill|Cheeger-Buser inequality|de|Cheeger-Buser-Ungleichung}} is named after him and [[Jeff Cheeger]].

He has been a professor at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (EPFL) since 1982. From 2004 to 2005 he was president of the [[Swiss Mathematical Society]]. In 2003 he was made an honorary doctor of the [[University of Helsinki]].
